subject: ELARA: Latency budgeting, throughput targets & cost levers
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: ELARA: Latency budgeting, throughput targets & cost levers

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion and helpful context. Summarizing what we captured and the concrete asks so we can align on a tight pilot scope. I attached a compact latency/throughput workbook and a one-page cost-levers PDF for quick reference.

Quick recap of what you asked us to validate:
- Target latency (user-perceived): p95 ≈ 300ms for short prompts (<= 64 tokens), p95 ≈ 700ms for longer completions (~512 tokens)
- Throughput: steady-state ~120 req/s, peak bursts to ~420 req/s for short windows during office hours
- Concurrency: expect 80 concurrent active users for the UI flows; orchestration for spike control is required
- Streaming: required for the transcript/playback feature (server-side partial tokens streamed to browser)
- Quality guardrail: you cannot accept more than ~2% reduction in top-1 accuracy on our labeled price-compare prompts

Proposed next steps (ask to Elara):
1) Confirm the two latency targets above and the 1M requests/month order of magnitude for cost modeling.
2) Grant us access to the small eval prompt set (redacted) or attach a representative CSV to the HubSpot record.
3) If procurement is ready, please loop procurement@elarahealth.com so we can include a pilot quote.

How Redwood will approach the pilot (summary):
- Start with a dedicated pilot cluster sized for 120 req/s (burst capacity configured up to 420 req/s)
- Run A/B: quantized 13B variant (q4) vs full-fp16 7B to balance latency and quality
- Apply continuous batching and prefix-KV caching for the UI flows to reduce per-token cost
- Streaming path will use smaller token buffer + reduced batch window to keep tail latency predictable

Attachments: elara_latency_budget_v1.xlsx (workbook with scenario tabs), redwood_cost-levers-summary.pdf

Please confirm the targets and whether we should include procurement on the next thread. Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma

nikhil@redwood.com

Subject: Re: ELARA: Latency budgeting, throughput targets & cost levers

Good questions — short answers and a couple of numbers to move procurement along.

Batching impact (typical):
- Continuous batching with a 10–25ms micro-window: p95 increases by ~15–40ms on short prompts but per-token cost drops ~25–45% depending on traffic shape.
- If you need strict p95 SLAs < 200ms we recommend a hybrid: immediate-path (no batching) for critical UI calls + batched path for analytics/async flows.

Quantization / quality:
- Observed top-1 delta on vertical prompts (our internal tests): q4 13B ≈ 0.8–1.6% relative accuracy drop vs fp16 13B; q4 13B still often beats fp16 7B on many semantic tasks. We'll run the 500-sample spot check you offered and share a short report within 48 hours.

Rough cost estimates (pilot-sized, includes serving + storage + networking; for 1M requests/month basis):
- q4 13B variant (continuous batching + prefix caching): ~$1,800–$2,400 per 1M requests
- fp16 7B (minimal quantization, faster per-token decode but fewer tokens cached): ~$2,700–$3,400 per 1M requests
Notes: estimates assume ~0.6 tokens per request on short prompts average; long-completion workloads will shift the numbers up. We can produce a line-item SOW for procurement.

What we'll deliver in the pilot:
- Two-week A/B run with the two model variants against the supplied prompt set
- Token-level cost breakdown and latency histograms (per-route)
- A failover policy that moves traffic to the cheaper variant automatically based on a quality threshold you set

Related links: https://hubspot.redwood/contacts/ELARA-9876 (I've added the sample prompts)

If that looks reasonable I'll loop procurement and propose a start date next week.

Thanks,
Nikhil

Subject: RE: ELARA: Latency budgeting, throughput targets & cost levers

Adding a quick technical note from the infra/solutions side — things we should checkpoint before pilot kickoff: 

1) Streaming + batching tradeoff:
- For server->browser streaming we recommend a small streaming buffer (3–5 tokens) and immediate flush for user-facing typing events. Large batch windows (>25ms) will harm perceived interactivity.

2) KV cache + memory footprint:
- Quantized 13B with a q4 path reduces memory per KV entry, which helps concurrency, but it does increase CPU effort on some hardware. We'll provision GPU memory headroom for your peak concurrency target (80 active users).

3) Autoscaling knobs:
- Recommend a two-tier policy: soft autoscale at 120 req/s (scale out pods), hard autoscale burst to capacity for 420 req/s for 90s windows. Include a circuit-breaker fallback to the cheaper model variant to prevent SLO breaches under extreme load.

4) Evaluation plan:
- Two-week A/B with a rolling quality monitor using your 500-sample checks. If q4 drops >2% compared to baseline, we trigger a canary rollback.

I'll prepare a short config snippet for the pilot cluster (batch window, stream buffer, cache TTL). Attaching the updated workbook tab with recommended pod counts.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
